title: Check websites concurrently
description: Implement a named function type called WebsiteChecker describing a check that receives a url and reports whether that site is ok. Then implement a function called CheckWebsites that receives a checker of that type together with a list of urls, and returns a lookup from url to whether that site is ok, holding one entry per url. For example, with a checker that considers every url ok except "waat://furhurterwe.geds": CheckWebsites(checker, ["http://google.com", "waat://furhurterwe.geds"]) -> {"http://google.com": true, "waat://furhurterwe.geds": false}. An empty list of urls produces an empty lookup. The checks must all run at the same time rather than one after another: start each url's check as its own concurrently running task, and have each task send its url together with that url's outcome back to the collecting code over a channel, bundling the two values together so they travel as one message. The collecting code then receives exactly as many messages as there were urls and records each one in the lookup. Do not write into the lookup from inside the concurrent tasks — several tasks writing to it at once is a data race — and do not pause for a fixed amount of time waiting for the tasks to finish.
objective: Practice running work concurrently and collecting its results safely over a channel instead of writing to shared state from several concurrent tasks.
